findings.claim: Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 044631bf, with the private overlay copied over the starter. The new isThisForm check (lines 25-29, used at line 42) identifies the submitted form by comparing each button's raw textContent with submitLabel. When it does not match, the listener returns without applying the fault and without failing closed, so this is the same silent class as edu-fcc-u1. I gave only a scratch copy of the solved form's submit button a decorative aria-hidden prefix. The button's accessible name stays 'Save service', so tests 1-7 and my correct test 8 still pass (Tests 8 passed (8)). npm test then exits 1 with three misses: blank-ignored, blank-saves and complete-ignored. Each tells the learner to add a check the test already makes, and the learner cannot fix it by changing the test. Nothing in the README or starter prompts a decorated button, so the trigger is unusual; this path was added in 044631bf.
findings.recommendation: Identify the form the way the learner's test finds the button: by role and accessible name within the submitted form, for example Testing Library's button-role query with the submitLabel name. Or fail closed on a mismatch, as readForm does. Add a decorated-button form to the private adversarial controls.

findings.claim: The fail-closed message is learner-safe and fails closed (observed: exit 1, one message, no false misses). Its remedy, 'Finish tasks 1-2 so every field has a label, then run npm test again', is reasoned never to be the true fix where it can print. The verifier runs only after the normal suite passes (lines 28-29), and that suite includes test 2, which has already found both labels on the same form with the same exact captions. The one trigger I could reach was a scratch form whose name caption is linked with aria-labelledby but sits outside the form element. That form passes test 2, the label query scoped to the form cannot see the caption, and the message told me to finish tasks 1-2, which were already done.
findings.recommendation: Reword for the state the learner is actually in, for example: the check could not find the 'Service name' and 'Owning team' fields inside the form your test submitted; keep each field's label inside the form element. Keep the fail-closed behaviour as it is.

findings.claim: This predates 044631bf and was not raised in earlier loops. The module teaches a visible required marker that the lab's exact-caption queries reject. accessible-forms artifact.md line 24 says 'Show required fields in the visible label text', and its worked example (line 75) is a label reading 'Phone (required)'. Line 42 repeats 'Mark required fields in the visible text'. README task 2 (lines 97-98) says only 'mark both required', and the starter TASK 2 comment narrows that to the required attribute (ServiceForm.jsx line 31). Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 044631bf, with the private overlay copied over the starter. With the solved form's name label changed to 'Service name (required)' in scratch, tests 2-8, including my correct learner test, failed: Test Files 7 failed | 1 passed (8), each with 'Unable to find a label with the text of: Service name'. A learner who follows the module's own example sees almost the whole suite fail. The message names the expected caption, so recovery is quick, and a learner who reads the TASK 2 comment avoids it.
findings.recommendation: In README task 2, say to mark both fields with the required attribute and keep the label text exactly 'Service name' and 'Owning team', because the tests find the fields by that text. Alternatively, have the tests accept a visible required marker. This does not justify a correction loop on its own.
